The probate solicitors growing their practice in 2026 have one thing in common.

They get there first.

Here is why being first matters more than being the best.

Every single day, the Gov.uk Probate Registry publishes new grants of probate. Each grant represents a family who has lost a loved one and now needs professional legal guidance. They need someone to handle the estate administration, manage the property sale, deal with inheritance tax, and guide them through a difficult process.

The solicitors who win these instructions are not necessarily the most experienced, the cheapest, or the most local. They are simply the ones who contact the executor first.

Here is what our data shows:

A probate practice that contacts an executor within 24 hours of a grant being issued wins instruction at a rate of over 30%. Wait 72 hours and that drops below 10%. Wait a week and you have effectively lost the opportunity to another firm.

9amLeads Probate alerts arrive in your inbox at 9am every morning. You see the deceased name, the estate value, the executor details, the grant type, and the registry location. Everything you need to make a professional and empathetic first contact.

A Manchester probate practice signed up for our alerts and picked up 4 new clients in their first month. Their annual subscription paid for itself 10 times over. Not because they undercut competitors on price. Because they reached out before any other firm knew the grant existed.

This is what first-mover advantage looks like in the probate market.

Like most accountants, he tried cold calling. He bought lists. He sent mailers. He spent hours every week reaching out to businesses that were not interested, did not need an accountant yet, or had already signed with someone else. His team was frustrated. His pipeline was unpredictable. His marketing budget was being spent on tactics that did not work.

Then he tried 9amLeads New Business Alerts.

In his first month, David signed 12 new clients. Twelve. Every single one came from a new company registration alert. Some were small one-person operations. Others were growing companies that needed full-service support. All of them were actively looking for help.

content:
The UK lead generation market is fundamentally broken. Here is why.

Platforms like Bark, Checkatrade, and RatedPeople operate on a business model that hurts the very businesses they claim to help. They sell the same lead to 3, 5, sometimes 10 businesses simultaneously. The customer receives multiple quotes and almost always picks the cheapest option. The businesses end up competing on price against each other instead of competing on quality, service, or trust.

This creates a race to the bottom where:
- Margins shrink on every job
- Your team spends hours quoting for leads they will not win
- Customers learn to expect cheaper prices because they know multiple businesses are bidding
- The quality of service declines because businesses need to cut costs to stay profitable

9amLeads exists because we believe businesses should not have to compete for the right to serve a customer.

Every lead we generate is sent to one business only. Yours. No other business in your area receives the same opportunity. You are the first and only person to contact that prospect.

The results speak for themselves:
